user.title: Set up HA Dev Tools
user.description:
Registers a `dev_tools` LLM API for Home Assistant's native `mcp_server` integration to serve. No configuration is needed here - tools stay disarmed until you run this on the Home Assistant host (via SSH or the Terminal add-on):

`date +%s > /config/.storage/ha_dev_tools.armed`

That arms it for up to 4 hours (extended by 30 minutes on each use, idle windows beyond 30 minutes expire it). Every tool call is also checked against the calling user's admin status - see the documentation link on this integration's page for why both gates exist.

abort.single_instance_allowed: HA Dev Tools is already configured. Only one instance is supported.

data_description.dry_run: When enabled, every write tool (write_automation, write_script, create/update/delete_helper, create/update/delete_derived_sensor, create/update/delete_template_entity, write_dashboard) is blocked - the tool call's own input is returned to the agent as a preview instead of being applied. Read-only tools and reload_domain/reload_derived_sensor/check_config are unaffected. For write_automation, write_script, and the template-entity tools, if git mirroring (below) is also enabled, the resolved would-be content is still pushed - to its own proposed branch (named after the write's kind and id) rather than to the mirror repo's default branch, since nothing live actually changed.
data_description.mirror_enabled: When enabled, a confirmed write from a supported tool (write_automation, write_script, create/update/delete_template_entity, write_dashboard, create/update/delete_helper, create/update/delete_derived_sensor) pushes the touched content's before/after state to the mirror repository below - a private, push-only audit trail and manual-rollback source, never the repo any deploy mechanism pulls from. Derived sensors have no real file, so their resolved config entry data/options are pushed to a synthetic path instead, and deleting one pushes a small deletion marker rather than removing anything. Content that looks like it contains a literal credential is never pushed. In dry-run mode (above), write_automation, write_script, and the template-entity tools push the resolved would-be content to a proposed branch (named after the write's kind and id) instead of the mirror repo's default branch, since nothing live changed; write_dashboard, the helper tools, and the derived-sensor tools have no such preview and push nothing while dry-run is on.
data_description.mirror_repo: A dedicated, private GitHub repository in owner/repo form. Deliberately separate from any repo a Git Pull-style add-on deploys from.
data_description.mirror_token: A fine-grained GitHub personal access token scoped to only the mirror repository above, with Contents: Read and write and nothing else - no workflow scope, no admin, an actual expiration date set.

mcp_server_not_exposing_dev_tools.title: dev_tools isn't reachable over MCP yet
mcp_server_not_exposing_dev_tools.description:
HA Dev Tools registers the `dev_tools` LLM API, but Home Assistant's own **Model Context Protocol Server** integration isn't loaded or isn't configured to expose it - so an MCP client currently gets a plain 404 instead of reaching any tool here.

To fix: **Settings → Devices & Services → Add Integration → Model Context Protocol Server** (if not already added), then add `dev_tools` to its exposed APIs. This issue clears itself automatically once that's done - no restart needed.
